system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: CORONA NCT00206310 - Crestor Versus Placebo in Subjects With Heart Failure
Investigational drug: rosuvastatin
Document: Investigating cardiovascular risk reduction--the Rosuvastatin GALAXY Programme (journal, published 2004-05-01, source pmid:15155117)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Investigating cardiovascular risk reduction--the Rosuvastatin GALAXY Programme

The GALAXY Programme is a comprehensive global research initiative that will address several important unanswered questions in statin research and investigate the impact of rosuvastatin on cardiovascular risk reduction and patient outcomes. Studies already completed demonstrate that rosuvastatin provides greater reductions in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) than other statins, enabling more patients to achieve LDL-C treatment goals. Additionally, rosuvastatin provides beneficial effects on other components of the atherogenic lipid profile. Ongoing studies will evaluate whether these effects translate into beneficial effects on atherosclerosis and significant reductions in cardiovascular events. Important information will also be provided on the role of statins in less well studied groups, including patients with heart failure, end stage renal disease, and individuals without elevated LDL-C but at heightened vascular risk as a result of increased systemic inflammation. Ultimately, the GALAXY Programme will provide clinical data that will enable physicians to make more effective statin treatment decisions, which will lead to improved patient care and cardiovascular outcomes.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
